title: OOM wave mitigation and cross-environment stale-cache compaction repair
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported recurring GPU OOMs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments over a 48-hour window. Root cause investigation points to interplay between allocator slab fragmentation under bursty prefix caching, and a KV cache tombstone accumulation that prevented timely compaction, leading to unbounded GPU memory growth for long-lived sessions. Impact: customer p99 latency spikes, failed inferences, and elevated error rates for high-concurrency models. Scope: affects both hosted pools with burst capacity and Dedicated nodes with mixed tenant workloads; private deployments observed similar behavior when prefix caching and session pinning were enabled.
comments: 2025-02-24: Incident triaged by on-call, initial mitigation: enforce per-session KV cache limit (soft throttle) and temporarily reduce max-concurrency for Hosted burst pools. Noted immediate reduction in new OOM reports but legacy sessions still trended upward.

2025-02-25: Heap profiler captures slab-growth pattern correlated with KV skiplist GC latencies. Hypothesis: tombstones created by aggressive prefix eviction were not reclaimed promptly due to GC scheduling being starved under high scheduling jitter.

2025-02-26: Core change proposed: introduce GC prioritization for KV tombstones plus a conservative allocator compaction pass triggered by memory-pressure heuristics. Design doc: https://confluence.company.internal/RT-oom-kv-frag-design (internal).

2025-02-27: Implemented runtime patch branch that (1) enforces per-session KV tombstone watermark and backpressure, (2) schedules incremental compaction when GPU resident memory delta exceeds threshold, and (3) adds allocator fence to avoid double-free during concurrent eviction. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8782

2025-02-28: QA: local reproducible test harness simulating 10k short-lived sessions validated compaction keeps resident set bounded and did not regress latency more than 3% at p50. Added unit + fuzz tests for concurrent GC paths.

2025-03-01: PR review feedback from @Elena Park: required clearer metrics emission for compaction cycles and a kill-switch config for private installs. Action: added metric names runtime.kv.compaction.cycles and runtime.alloc.compaction_seconds, and feature flag runtime.compaction.enable (defaults true).

2025-03-02: Canary rollout started to 5% of Hosted, and to one Dedicated pool; observed zero new OOMs in canary and steady lower memory growth. Private customer partner applied patch to staging and validated with their load generator.

2025-03-03: Preparing release notes and cadence for broader rollout. Post-release tasks: instrument long-tail memory diagnostics for 30 days, schedule follow-up to evaluate sustained fragmentation below 1% across pools.
